(existing Cooking inference Python) -> existing Qwen3-VL-8B NF4 backend ->
working Cooking interpreter **read-only**, configurable via GATEWAY_INFERENCE_PYTHON.
Cooking environment. You can point it to a separately provisioned environment with
the same pinned inference dependencies. No package is installed into Cooking.
Imports only app.services modules, never Cooking CLI/application entry points.
cache/temp directories prevent writes to Cooking or model downloads. The new
Python package is ai_gateway, so it does not shadow Cooking's app package.
- app.services.vision_backend_registry.create_backend
- app.services.qwen8b_nf4_backend.Qwen8BNF4Backend
- app.services.qwen4b_nf4_backend.Qwen4BNF4Backend.generate_profiled / close
- app.services.vision_optimization.parse
- app.services.dedicated_worker.baseline_gate / postload_gate
It does not construct or weaken Cooking's image-required VisionRequest. The existing
F:\Cooking-AI-review\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -B -m venv .venv
storage inside Cooking. The default model path points to the existing 8B directory.
also locks byte 0 of the **existing** Cooking jobs/.speech_gpu.lock using a read-only
handle, compatible with Cooking's filelock. It never creates/removes that file.
Because Cooking removes its lock after a task, default shared mode may intentionally
remain unavailable. Do not start a Cooking task merely to manufacture this lock.
Dedicated mode is a scheduling commitment: no Cooking/other GPU workloads may start
while the service is alive. If a Cooking lock already exists, it is still respected.
